top.title: Treat gunshot victims first; police report can wait – IGP Disu to doctors
top.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The Inspector General of Police, Tunji Disu, has urged hospitals and healthcare workers across the country to treat gunshot victims immediately without demanding police reports, warning that delays could cost lives. Disu also called on members of the public to assist injured persons in accessing medical attention, assuring them that they would not face punishment for helping victims. The IGP made the appeal in a sensitisation message by the National Orientation Agency (NOA) in collaboration with the Nigeria Police Force, shared by the police on its X account on Thursday. Addressing Nigerians, police officers and medical personnel, Disu described the treatment of gunshot victims as a matter of life and death, stressing that no police documentation was required before emergency medical care could be provided. “Fellow Nigerians, I am here to address a matter of life and death – the treatment of gunshot victims in our hospitals. “To my fellow officers, to my medical personnel across the nation, and to every Nigerian listening, treating gunshot victims does not require a police report. “When a gunshot victim is brought to any hospital, the law does not require a police report before treatment,” he said. He urged doctors and other healthcare workers to prioritise saving lives rather than allow administrative procedures to delay emergency treatment. “To our doctors and healthcare workers, you are enjoined to treat gunshot victims immediately without waiting for a police report. Our duty is not to create fear but to protect lives. We wish to reassure citizens of their safety at all times,” Disu added. The police chief also appealed to Nigerians not to hesitate to help people who sustain gunshot injuries, emphasising that the law protects those who assist victims. “To the members of the public, if you see someone injured, do not hesitate to help. You will not be punished for helping. “Again, to my officers and medical personnel, please uphold the law because every second counts. Treat first, save lives,” he said. In a related message accompanying the video, the Nigeria Police Force warned that refusing or delaying medical attention for gunshot victims was punishable under the Compulsory Treatment and Care for Victims of Gunshots Act, 2017. According to the police, the legislation requires all public and private hospitals to provide immediate treatment to gunshot victims, regardless of whether they have police reports or clearance. The police further warned that violations of the Act could attract imprisonment of up to 15 years and other penalties, depending on the offence. The law provides that every hospital in Nigeria, whether public or private, must receive and provide immediate and adequate treatment to anyone with gunshot wounds, with or without police clearance. It also places a responsibility on members of the public, including security personnel, to assist victims and ensure they are taken to the nearest hospital for treatment

top.title: Nonprofit Common Space will launch 1st 'humanitarian satellite' in 2027
top.description: null The first satellite in a constellation designed for humanitarian use will lift off next year, if all goes according to plan. The nonprofit Common Space plans to assemble a six-spacecraft constellation of Earth-observing satellites , whose high-resolution imagery will aid first responders, journalists, scientists and human-rights investigators around the world. That plan firmed up a bit today (Nov. 19), as Common Space announced the builder of the first of those satellites : Satellogic, an Argentine-U.S. geospatial intelligence company. There are more than 1,000 Earth-observing satellites circling our planet at the moment. But much of the data they gather is proprietary or too expensive to serve the common good, according to Common Space. The nonprofit wants to change that via its envisioned constellation, which it says will collect imagery specifically for humanitarian and public-interest purposes. Common Space plans to operate on a "club-good model," which will share infrastructure and costs across a large community, allowing extensive, low-cost access to high-quality imagery. Satellogic is now officially part of this picture. "With Satellogic as our spacecraft partner, we're moving from vision to orbit and putting high-resolution data into the hands of those who need it most," Common Space co-founder Rhiannan Price said in a statement today. "This isn't just another satellite. We're building infrastructure to serve people for years to come." The satellite is Satellogic's NewSat Mark V, which Common Space selected after a competitive request-for-proposal process. Satellites can help first responders deal with natural disasters. Here, one of Vantor's Earth-imaging satellites captures the destruction Hurricane Melissa caused to Black River, in southwest Jamaica, in November 2025. (Image credit: Vantor Technologies/CC BY 4.0) The NewSat Mark V is just 32 inches (82 centimeters) long and weighs 85 pounds (38.5 kilograms) here on Earth . But the microsatellite packs a great deal of capability into that small package. From low Earth orbit (LEO), it naturally resolves features on the ground as small as 27.5 inches (70 cm), which Satellogic's proprietary algorithms can boost to a "super resolution" of 19.7 inches (50 cm). The satellite is scheduled to launch in July 2027 on a SpaceX rideshare mission. Satellogic will handle the preparations for that launch and manage satellite operations, which are expected to last at least five years in LEO. The company has extensive experience with such work; it has flown 61 of its Earth-observing satellites to date, all of which deployed successfully. And Satellogic is aligned with Common Space philosophically, the company stressed. "Common Space shares our belief that persistent global intelligence shouldn't be reserved for a few. top.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nigerian music stars Burna Boy, Asake and Seyi Vibez have secured spots on the soundtrack of the highly anticipated video game, Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI). The Nigerian artistes are among several international performers featured on the game’s soundtrack, which was recently unveiled by Rockstar Games, the developer of the popular gaming franchise. Among the Nigerian tracks featured on the station are Asake’s ‘Joha’ and ‘Giza’, a collaboration between Burna Boy and Seyi Vibez. The station’s previewed playlist also includes ‘Gye Wani’ by Pat Thomas featuring Ebo Taylor, as well as ‘Shay’sana’ by DJ Lag and Robot Boii featuring Kamo Mphela. Burna Boy also makes a separate contribution to the game’s official soundtrack with his song ‘Bigger’. Other international artistes featured on the soundtrack include Travis Scott, Dua Lipa, Cardi B, Gunna, Young Thug, Kodak Black, Don Toliver, Zara Larsson, Camila Cabello and Lana Del Rey. The development marks another international gaming appearance for Nigerian music, as Afrobeats continues to gain visibility across global entertainment platforms. top.title: Parents: please don’t buy Grand Theft Auto VI for your child
top.description: Rockstar Games’ brilliant 18-rated criminal caper is stuffed with sex, drugs and violence. It is the most explicit game I’ve ever played – and it really is not for kids I am haunted still by an interaction I had at my stepson’s ninth birthday party in 2014, where one of the kids asked if I could put on Grand Theft Auto V for them all. “I have it at home!”, he said, giving me the puppy-dog eyes. Mentally replaying that game in my head, flashing back to the many scenes involving such things as smoking meth, over-the-top gratuitous violence and grubby sex in one character’s trailer, I said “ no way” . Later I gently mentioned to the kid’s mother that GTA V was an 18-rated game and really wasn’t suitable for kids. “Oh, but he’s really good at these games,” she told me. She was genuinely shocked to learn that an 18-rating on a video game was a flag for adult content, rather than an indication of its difficulty. Grand Theft Auto VI is released this week. It is an incredible creative and technical feat, conjuring a realistic-looking and exhaustively detailed virtual Florida filled with every kind of filth and criminality you could imagine. It is brilliant, entertainingly observed and even sometimes unexpectedly touching, largely thanks to a central love story between the player couple , Jason and Lucia. It is lewd, violent and frequently hilarious. It is also absolutely full of stuff that I really would not want my 10 and seven-year-old boys to see or hear. I have never played a game that has more thoroughly earned its 18 rating. Continue reading...

top.title: China, US, Russia issue ‘peace declaration’ after first summit
top.description: China, the United States and Russia issued a “peace declaration” Thursday following an unprecedented leaders’ summit, almost five years into the Ukraine war and with Donald Trump bogged down in Iran. The statement after Xi Jinping, Trump and Vladimir Putin met in China, said that they wanted to reform the United Nations, to protect diplomatic immunity and boost supply and production of refined petroleum products. “The three heads of state engaged in an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed themselves to upholding strategic stability and international security,” said the statement published by Chinese state media and the Kremlin, but not yet by the White House. The three-way meeting took place with Russia’s years-long offensive in Ukraine grinding on, mayhem in the Middle East in the wake of Trump’s attacks on Iran, and an ascendant China looking to strengthen its hand in East Asia. “Our countries have many converging interests when it comes to resolving regional conflicts, including, of course, the conflict in Ukraine,” Putin said at the start of the meeting, adding they had a “shared responsibility for maintaining international peace and security”. The three men made opening remarks touching on weighty topics from nuclear weapons to the war in Ukraine as they met around a large, dark round table with a pink flower arrangement at its centre. The discussion behind closed doors in Kylin Villa in Shenzhen ended after an hour and 20 minutes. Trump said the three men were “making history”, while Putin said they wrote a new “page in the history of diplomacy”. “The three countries share a common perspective on safeguarding world peace,” Xi said. ICC, UN and oil In their joint statement, the leaders agreed that “the International Criminal Court and other similar institutions must not abuse their jurisdiction.” Putin is subject to an ICC arrest warrant while Trump’s administration has vowed to dismantle the court “brick by brick”. The leaders also “acknowledged the vital importance of the principle of state consent and the respect for (diplomatic) immunity enjoyed by state officials”, the statement said, adding that each country was “committed” to advancing the reform of the United Nations. Putin said the discussion would also touch on food and energy security – both of which have been upended by conflicts in Iran and Ukraine. nigeria.title: FIFA chief Infantino faces challenge from France’s Diallo, Japan’s Tashima
nigeria.description: French football chief Philippe Diallo and veteran Japanese official Kozo Tashima were on Thursday confirmed by FIFA as the challengers to incumbent Gianni Infantino in next year’s presidential election. Infantino has faced criticism over his aborted plan to allow private investment into the World Cup, but he retains considerable support for his bid to win re-election next March. French Football Federation president Diallo will represent UEFA, the European confederation which has been the most vocal in its criticism of Infantino. Tashima is a former head of the Japan Football Association and has served on the FIFA Council. FIFA said the candidacies will be examined by the body’s electoral committee before a final decision is made on whether to admit them. nigeria.description: Former Super Eagles coach, Jo Bonfrere, has warned that Nigeria could miss out on the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations if the team fails to improve its performance in the remaining qualifying matches. Bonfrere gave the warning following Nigeria’s goalless draw against Tanzania’s Taifa Stars in Zanzibar on Tuesday, a result he described as a setback to the country’s qualification campaign. The result left the three-time African champions second in Group L with seven points from four matches, three points behind leaders Guinea-Bissau, who defeated Madagascar 2-0 in Bissau. With only group winners guaranteed qualification for the tournament, the former coach said Nigeria must win their remaining fixtures to avoid putting their AFCON hopes in jeopardy. Speaking to Complete Sports, Bonfrere said the Super Eagles missed an opportunity to close the gap on Guinea-Bissau with a victory in Zanzibar. “It’s a poor result for the Super Eagles,” he said. “The Super Eagles should have done better. Bonfrere, who led Nigeria’s U-23 team to football gold at the 1996 Olympic Games in Atlanta, Georgia, also expressed concern over the team’s scoring record in the qualifiers. Nigeria have scored five goals and conceded the same number in four Group L matches, a record the Dutch tactician said was below expectations, considering the quality of players available to the country. He argued that the Super Eagles should be scoring more goals, given that several members of the squad feature for top European clubs. “You score goals, you win games. If you don’t score, you don’t win. The Super Eagles have good players in top European teams. They have more experience than any other team in Africa. So, they must score goals,” he said. Comparing Nigeria’s performance with that of Guinea-Bissau, Bonfrere noted that the group leaders had scored eight goals and conceded just one in their four matches. “You said Guinea-Bissau have scored eight goals and conceded one. That’s good for them. That’s what the Super Eagles should be doing, and even more, because Nigeria have quality players,” he added. nigeria.title: AI being run in a ‘mediaeval’ way – UN
nigeria.description: Artificial intelligence is being governed in an almost mediaeval fashion, the UN rights chief warned Thursday, with power concentrated in the hands of a few tech barons. Speaking at the RightsX summit in Geneva, Volker Turk said that while the story of AI sounded futuristic, underneath it was an age-old narrative of power. “A handful of men still control much of the world’s AI computing power, data and infrastructure. And we still have no common rules to pace or steer AI development,” he said. Turk said there was a glaring democratic deficit when five technology companies owned more than 70 percent of global AI computing capacity. “We have the technology of the future governed in an almost mediaeval way: by a select few, with virtually no checks, no balances, no participation, and no accountability,” he said. “History has taught us: with this kind of power, the rights and freedoms of ordinary people are the first to suffer.” Reiterating his call for rights-centred AI regulation, the UN high commissioner for human rights said the technology was increasingly controlling people’s lives. And this, he warned, was often happening without their knowledge, and could distort public debate in “subtle, insidious ways”. Meanwhile biased algorithms could reproduce injustice on an industrial scale, he cautioned. – ‘Civilisational collapse’ – “Our transport, food and healthcare are increasingly digitised. We may not be far from the day when AI can cut off the critical infrastructure of entire communities or countries, either on its own or in the wrong hands,” Turk warned. “When people discuss the chances of civilisational collapse because of AI, we need to ask: who decides what chances we take?” He voiced optimism that people would ultimately challenge unchecked power, with the democratic deficit turning into a deficit of trust. He cited young people already stepping offline to regain greater control of their lives. Turk said AI’s benefits should be shared equitably, which would require goodwill from technology companies, but also regulation and accountability. He said he had written to frontier AI companies urging them to introduce effective safeguards “before it is too late”. Turk noted that a bottle of milk could not make it to a shop without layers of testing, rules and regulations. So for AI, “it’s a no-brainer that you need some form of regulation”, given its potential for harm, Turk said. entertainment.title: From Tunde Kelani to Akinola Davies Jr., 5 Nollywood Directors You Should Know
entertainment.description: From music visuals to international festival stages and actor-turned-director debuts, Dammy Twitch, Akinola Davies Jr., and Daniel Etim Effiong represent different paths into Nollywood directing. Think about the Nigerian films and series you have watched recently, the ones that kept you glued to your screen, had you talking about the storyline long after the credits rolled or recommending them to everyone you know. While the actors are often the faces you remember first, there is someone behind the camera whose creative choices help bring those stories to life: the director. From interpreting the script and guiding actors to shaping how each scene looks, sounds and unfolds, directors influence almost every part of what ends up on screen. As Nollywood grows in ambition, production quality and global reach, the filmmakers steering these projects are becoming just as central to the industry’s story as the stars in front of the lens. Some have spent decades bringing Nigerian literature and history to the screen, while others are earning international acclaim or crossing over from music videos into feature films. Here are five Nollywood directors whose work is worth knowing. Tunde Kelani Start with Tunde Kelani if you want to see where modern Nigerian cinema found its literary and cultural roots. Trained at the London Film School after cutting his teeth in photography and television, the Mainframe Films founder has spent decades turning Nigerian literature, stage plays, and history into lasting screen works. Titles like Ti Oluwa Nile , Koseegbe , O Le Ku , Saworoide , Thunderbolt: Magun , The Narrow Path , Maami , Dazzling Mirage , Ayinla , and Cordelia show how wide his range goes. Across years of festivals and awards, Kelani has collected major honours for his craft, and his adaptation Cordelia earned him a Best Director nomination at the 2026 Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards. Tunde Kelani, whose directing catalogue spans Ti Oluwa Nile, Saworoide, The Narrow Path, Maami, and Cordelia, with Kunle Afolayan outdoors. Photo Credit: Tunde Kelani/Instagram Akinola Davies Jr. Few directors have linked global festival stages with homegrown Nollywood triumphs quite like Akinola Davies Jr. After his short film Lizard won the Short Film Grand Jury Prize at the Sundance Film Festival in 2021, he co-wrote and directed his feature debut My Father’s Shadow alongside his brother Wale Davies . The drama made history in 2025 as the first Nigerian film selected for the Official Selection at the Cannes Film Festival, picking up a Special Mention for the Caméra d’Or before winning Best Director at the British Independent Film Awards and Breakthrough Director at the Gotham Independent Film Awards. His momentum rolled straight into 2026 with a BAFTA win for Outstanding Debut by a British Writer, Director or Producer, followed by Best Director and Best Overall Movie wins at the 2026 AMVCAs. entertainment.title: Esther Adeyanju: This International Men’s Day, Let’s Make Room for Men’s Vulnerability
entertainment.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. But if a man struggles to achieve all these, is his life any less meaningful? Surely, a man’s worth cannot be reduced to his bank balance, job title or ability to convince everyone that he has everything under control. There must be room for men who are still becoming. entertainment.title: Burna Boy, Asake & Seyi Vibez Bring Afrobeats to the World of GTA VI
entertainment.description: From left: Nigerian artists Asake, Seyi Vibez, and Burna Boy, whose songs appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. How else could Grand Theft Auto VI begin than with Nigerian artists featured in the music lineup of the biggest video game release of the year? As players around the world finally step into Rockstar Games’ highly anticipated open-world action-adventure title, Burna Boy , Asake , and Seyi Vibez are making sure Nigerian music is front and centre on the virtual streets of Vice City and the wider state of Leonida. Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) officially arrives today, Thursday, 19 November 2026, on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, ending a 13-year wait since Grand Theft Auto V first hit consoles. Developed and published by Rockstar Games, the open-world action-adventure game follows dual protagonists Jason and Lucia across the sun-soaked, neon-lit state of Leonida—a fictional take on Florida that brings players back to Vice City in the franchise’s largest map yet. Music has always been at the heart of the Grand Theft Auto universe, where players tune into curated in-game radio stations while driving or walking around town, and this sixth instalment takes African soundscapes seriously. At the centre of the Nigerian presence is AfroBank FM, a dedicated African music radio station inside Grand Theft Auto VI that is co-hosted by Grammy winner Burna Boy—credited on-air simply as Burna—alongside British DJ and producer Palms Trax , who goes by Palmsy. Curated to spotlight everything from 20th-century African classics to contemporary Afrobeats, amapiano, and 3-step, the station features Asake’s 2022 hit “ Joha ” from his debut album Mr Money With The Vibe , as well as “ Giza “, the 2023 collaboration between Burna Boy and Seyi Vibez from Burna Boy’s seventh studio album I Told Them …. Alongside those tracks, Burna Boy also appears on the game’s official companion soundtrack album, Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album, with his original song “ Bigger ” sitting on a 34-track roster that includes Travis Scott , Cardi B , Dua Lipa , SZA , Tame Impala , and Lana Del Rey . The African representation on AfroBank FM stretches beyond Nigeria too, sharing airwaves with Ghanaian highlife legends Pat Thomas and Ebo Taylor on “ Gye Wani ” and South African stars DJ Lag , Robot Boii , and Kamo Mphela on “ Shay’sana “. With players able to listen to Leonida’s terrestrial radio stations both in vehicles and on foot through in-game headphones, millions of gamers worldwide are now cruising through Vice City with Burna Boy on the mic and Asake and Seyi Vibez on heavy rotation. entertainment.title: How La Roche-Posay Brought Skin Science to Over 500 Guests in Its First Living Lab Experience
entertainment.description: La Roche-Posay concluded its first Living Lab experience in Nigeria, welcoming Nigerian stakeholders to its opening party and three-day programme, held from 4 to 6 November 2026 at Oasis by The Five Palm, Victoria Island, Lagos. Inspired by the original Living Lab concept in Paris, the experience brought the science, research and expertise behind skincare closer to Nigerian consumers and healthcare professionals. It marked the brand’s first Living Lab in the country, creating a platform for more accessible conversations around skin health, dermatological innovation and everyday skincare. The experience opened with an exclusive session for healthcare professionals and invited guests before welcoming members of the public over the following two days. Each day featured three expert-led sessions exploring the role of dermatology and scientific research in advancing skin health, the wider impact of skin conditions on everyday life, and the importance of understanding product safety, tolerance and efficacy. The sessions brought together healthcare professionals and representatives from across Nigeria’s dermatological beauty and skincare community, encouraging knowledge-sharing and stronger connections between science, expertise and consumer education. Visitors explored five dedicated Innovation Corners showcasing La Roche-Posay’s Effaclar, Mela B3, Anthelios, Cicaplast and Lipikar ranges. Each space introduced visitors to specific skin concerns and the science behind the brand’s product formulations. Through interactive demonstrations and guided product experiences, guests gained a better understanding of different skin concerns and the role of targeted skincare in addressing them. At the Anthelios corner, visitors used a UV camera to see the effects of ultraviolet exposure and better understand the importance of sun protection. The Effaclar and Mela B3 spaces explored concerns including blemishes and hyperpigmentation, while the Cicaplast and Lipikar corners introduced visitors to approaches to caring for sensitive, damaged and dry skin. Beyond the Innovation Corners, visitors explored the Blue House, which presented La Roche-Posay’s history and commitment to dermatological innovation, and the Scars of Life Cinema. The cinema screened a 25-minute film exploring the physical and psychological realities of living with scars and scarring, including their impact on self-image and everyday life. The film also highlighted how Lipikar supports the care of skin affected by scarring, bringing attention to the importance of addressing both the visible and less visible experiences associated with skin conditions. The programme also created opportunities for visitors to engage with skincare experts and dermatologists through one-on-one consultations, ask questions about their individual skin concerns and receive guidance on building appropriate skincare routines. entertainment.title: International Men’s Day: Six Films That Explore the Vulnerable Side of Men
entertainment.description: One of the best aspects of art is its ability to imitate current events or imagine possibilities. Movies, as a powerful art form, present a sequence of events that allows viewers to see reflections of themselves or envision who they could become. At its core, art exists to entertain, inform and critique society. Through films, music and visual expressions, we are continually reminded of our shared humanity—our joys, flaws and contradictions. One subject that art, particularly film, has explored is masculinity. However, this theme is often addressed subtly and can be easy to overlook, as the movies that dominate global box offices frequently focus on spectacle: fantasy, romance, adventure or others. Conversations about men, their inner lives, vulnerabilities and social roles are often not in the top circle. Nonetheless, some films have attempted to explore what it means to be a man in today’s world. They invite audiences to contemplate important questions such as: What is the role of men in society? What defines a man? How does a man’s behaviour influence those around him? What expectations does society place on men? What responsibilities do men have within society? Where does responsibility begin, and where does it end? Do men matter? Do their feelings matter? The theme for this year’s International Men’s Day is “The Future Is For Everyone.” For that, here are some movies that explore and illuminate the complexities of masculinity: The Pursuit of Happyness This classic film reveals the vulnerability often hidden behind male perseverance. Will Smith ’s portrayal of Chris Gardner challenges the stoic notion of manhood by showing fatherhood as both an act of love and endurance. Through his struggles with homelessness, rejection, and exhaustion, the film redefines masculinity, depicting it as the courage to remain tender even when life tests your strength in every way. Fatherhood Kevin Hart ’s film Fatherhood delves into themes of grief and single parenthood, balancing humour with heartfelt moments. It challenges traditional expectations of masculinity by illustrating a father’s journey through uncertainty, learning empathy, and committing to being present for his child/ren. Through this film, Kevin Hart shares his vision of what it means to be a man and a father. Adolescence Adolescence examines how boys internalise distorted notions of strength and freedom, and how escaping them demands emotional awareness. entertainment.title: Beyoncé Becomes First Artist in Grammy History to Earn 100 Nominations!
entertainment.description: Beyoncé becomes the first artist in history to reach 100 career Grammy nominations. Photo Credit: Beyoncé/Instagram If you have ever wondered what triple digits look like on music’s biggest stage, Beyoncé just gave everyone the answer. The Houston-born global music superstar has officially become the first artist in history to reach 100 career Grammy nominations, hitting the milestone with her latest nod for “ Morning Dew ( Donk )”, which is nominated for Best R&B Solo Performance at the 69th Annual Grammy Awards (2027 Grammys). Released in July 2026 ahead of the 20th anniversary of her sophomore album B’Day, “Morning Dew (Donk)” puts her in a category alongside Kehlani , Victoria Monét , Jill Scott , and Nigerian star Tems . To put the 100-nomination milestone into perspective, no other recording artist has ever crossed into triple digits since the Grammys began. Beyoncé had previously been tied with her husband, Jay-Z , at 88 nominations each before breaking that tie in 2024 with 11 nods for Cowboy Carter to reach 99—and this latest recognition pushes her even further ahead as the artist with the highest number of Grammy nominations in history. Beyoncé holding her three Grammy trophies at the 67th Annual Grammy Awards in 2025. Photo Credit: Beyoncé/Instagram It is also a good reminder of how long she has been doing this at the highest level. Beyoncé’s Grammy journey started all the way back in 2000 as part of Destiny’s Child with “Bills, Bills, Bills”, and across more than two decades as a solo artist, group member, and collaborator, she has built a record that keeps stretching further ahead of the pack. Alongside holding the title for the most Grammy nominations of all time, she is already the most awarded artist in Grammy history with 35 wins, a record she first broke in 2023 when she surpassed late conductor Georg Solti ’s 31 trophies. She pushed that tally even higher at the 2025 Grammys, taking home three awards—Album of the Year and Best Country Album for Cowboy Carter, as well as Best Country Duo/Group Performance for “II Most Wanted” alongside Miley Cyrus . Now all eyes turn to Sunday, 7 February 2027, when the 2027 Grammy Awards take place at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles and we find out whether nomination number 100 turns into Grammy win number 36. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. Mentally replaying that game in my head, flashing back to the many scenes involving such things as smoking meth, over-the-top gratuitous violence and grubby sex in one character’s trailer, I said “ no way” . technology.title: How to tell a cyberattack from a plain old outage
technology.description: Over the past week, anyone could be forgiven for wondering whether a Diehard IV –style cyberwar had finally arrived in the US. Across just four consecutive business days, a mass Microsoft exchange outage broke IT services for thousands of companies , a Federal Aviation Administration tech screw-up grounded airplanes across the country, a software problem affecting JPMorgan Chase caused another round of disruption, a United Airlines system glitch delayed flights yet again, and an NSA classified network’s downtime left the agency’s staff sitting at home waiting to return to their office at Fort Meade. In the midst of a US war with Iran and rising fears of AI-enabled hacking , this still-unfolding comedy of IT errors colliding across American infrastructure felt to plenty of observers like more than a coincidence. Yet there’s still no evidence that any one of these clustered technological failures were related, much less caused by hackers. Their improbable, sequential timing left Americans anxiously doomscrolling for signs of foul play. But in cases like these, it’s the job of cybersecurity analysts (and reporters at WIRED) to determine—vibes aside—whether the latest tech outage was actually an accident or the result of a cyberattack. science.title: Nonprofit Common Space will launch 1st 'humanitarian satellite' in 2027
science.description: null The first satellite in a constellation designed for humanitarian use will lift off next year, if all goes according to plan. The nonprofit Common Space plans to assemble a six-spacecraft constellation of Earth-observing satellites , whose high-resolution imagery will aid first responders, journalists, scientists and human-rights investigators around the world. That plan firmed up a bit today (Nov. 19), as Common Space announced the builder of the first of those satellites : Satellogic, an Argentine-U.S. geospatial intelligence company. There are more than 1,000 Earth-observing satellites circling our planet at the moment. But much of the data they gather is proprietary or too expensive to serve the common good, according to Common Space. The nonprofit wants to change that via its envisioned constellation, which it says will collect imagery specifically for humanitarian and public-interest purposes. Common Space plans to operate on a "club-good model," which will share infrastructure and costs across a large community, allowing extensive, low-cost access to high-quality imagery. Satellogic is now officially part of this picture. "With Satellogic as our spacecraft partner, we're moving from vision to orbit and putting high-resolution data into the hands of those who need it most," Common Space co-founder Rhiannan Price said in a statement today. "This isn't just another satellite. We're building infrastructure to serve people for years to come." The satellite is Satellogic's NewSat Mark V, which Common Space selected after a competitive request-for-proposal process. Satellites can help first responders deal with natural disasters. Here, one of Vantor's Earth-imaging satellites captures the destruction Hurricane Melissa caused to Black River, in southwest Jamaica, in November 2025. (Image credit: Vantor Technologies/CC BY 4.0) The NewSat Mark V is just 32 inches (82 centimeters) long and weighs 85 pounds (38.5 kilograms) here on Earth . But the microsatellite packs a great deal of capability into that small package. From low Earth orbit (LEO), it naturally resolves features on the ground as small as 27.5 inches (70 cm), which Satellogic's proprietary algorithms can boost to a "super resolution" of 19.7 inches (50 cm). The satellite is scheduled to launch in July 2027 on a SpaceX rideshare mission. Satellogic will handle the preparations for that launch and manage satellite operations, which are expected to last at least five years in LEO. The company has extensive experience with such work; it has flown 61 of its Earth-observing satellites to date, all of which deployed successfully. And Satellogic is aligned with Common Space philosophically, the company stressed. "Common Space shares our belief that persistent global intelligence shouldn't be reserved for a few. science.title: What's next for NASA interstellar Voyager 1 probe after passing 1 light-day from Earth?
science.description: null Voyager 1 has reached a historic milestone in space — it now takes a light-day to send a command to the spacecraft, meaning a full 24 hours for Earth to hail the distant spacecraft. Since Voyager 1 and its twin, Voyager 2 , launched on an initial tour through the outer solar system in 1977, their missions have been packed with science. Voyager 1 looked at Jupiter and Saturn from up close before veering for a flyby of Saturn's moon Titan and Saturn's rings, a pathway that brought it above the plane of the solar system in the early 1980s. Voyager 1's faster path out of the solar system brought it to one light-day in distance on Wednesday (Nov. 18), while Voyager 2 — which took a slightly slower track to see Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune — will reach a light-day of distance in 2035. So what's next for the two Voyager spacecraft as they reach further into interstellar space? Exploring afar Interstellar space, which is the area where the sun's constant stream of solar particles within the heliopause gives way to the physics of interstellar space, has been a valuable harvest for both Voyagers. Voyager 1 crossed interstellar space in August 2012 and continues to get data, while Voyager 2 has done the same since November 2018. "Current science is continuing our investigation on magnetic field strength and direction, plasma density, and energetic particle detection. What is important is to measure how these phenomena change as the spacecraft travels further away from the sun," Suzanne Dodd, project manager for the Voyager missions at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), told Space.com in an email. Added to that will be the Voyagers' examinations of plasma and magnetic fields nearby the spacecraft, and a focus on any "solar effects" such as shocks or pressure fronts, added JPL project scientist Linda Spilker in an email. "Key Voyager science going forward includes observing the extent to which our sun continues to affect interstellar space, all the way out to Voyager 1," Spilker continued. "Where does the sun's influence end and pristine interstellar space begin? Perhaps Voyager may last long enough to answer that question." The team also wants to watch the magnetic field around the spacecraft continue to change direction from the sun, to interstellar space, Spilker noted. That finding was not expected when the Voyagers launched, so scientists are curious to know more — as long as the spacecraft can last, that is. science.title: How aquanauts could help save Florida’s reefs
science.description: It sounds idyllic. Who wouldn’t want to occupy a newly built residence in the Florida Keys, complete with its own coral garden right outside the window? The only complication is that it is 17 metres below the surface of the Atlantic Ocean. That is not putting off Jim Brittsan, though. “This is really exciting,” he says. Brittsan is the founder and executive director of coral restoration non-profit Sustainable Ocean and Reefs (SOAR). He is also the diver who arranged the temporary coral nursery beside the residence, having brought the corals from a site where, 10 metres closer to the surface, they faced increasing environmental stress. Now, in reduced temperatures, they are starting to flourish, hosting their own marine life – visible day and night, in all its busyness, from the underwater residence known as Vanguard just 15 metres away. Vanguard was deployed at Tennessee Reef in June 2026 DEEP and Brendan Hall Vanguard is a long-stay underwater station for marine biologists. It was deployed in June 2026 at Tennessee Reef on the seafloor of the Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary, around 8 kilometres south of Long Key. Its coral nursery looks like a strange marine shrubbery: the coral fragments are arranged on anchored ropes that stand upright in the water. Once Vanguard is operational, a more permanent nursery will be established and the corals will eventually be planted on the seabed as part of ongoing restoration efforts, with their long-term survival assessed through monitoring. Advertisement Resident scientists will be able to monitor marine life around the clock DEEP, the international design and engineering organisation that built Vanguard, aims to make humans aquatic by establishing more subsea habitats like it. These will allow people to live underwater for extended periods to engage in scientific research and conservation. This opens up unprecedented opportunities to do research because there is no need for divers to bounce up and down to a research vessel on the surface. Those round trips eat into valuable work hours, because divers can spend only limited time at depth and must ascend slowly to avoid decompression sickness. “If we’re diving from a boat, we can do about 3 hours’ work a day at depth,” Brittsan says. “It’s much more efficient if we can just stay down there.” Corals moved to deeper, cooler water beside Vanguard are recovering in a temporary nursery DEEP There is plenty of work to do in the Florida Keys. Elkhorn (Acropora palmata) and staghorn (Acropora cervicornis) corals, which are vital reef-building species, are now considered functionally extinct in Florida. But it is not just in Florida waters that corals are struggling. Climate change, which brings elevated ocean temperatures, is a significant threat to corals around the world. science.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 19 – The… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Original Annotated The Horsehead and Flame Nebulas Explanation: Today’s image could have been a painting. But what do these colors mean? The brightest star, left of the center, is blue Alnitak (the Girdle): a triple star system best known for being the easternmost star in Orion’s Belt . The instantly recognizable shape of a dark horse’s head at the center is the aptly named Horsehead Nebula . It is about five light-years tall and lies approximately 1,500 light-years away. It is made of dust and gas that obscure the red glow behind it, which is caused by hydrogen gas being ionized by the bright star Sigma Orionis at the top. science.description: Turmeric capsules are touted as remedies for joint problems olga Yastremska/Alamy Turmeric supplements seem to have little to no effect on pain and mobility problems caused by knee osteoarthritis. That’s according to one of the most rigorous assessments of the evidence yet, which focused on four randomised controlled trials comparing the supplements to placebo pills. Osteoarthritis, which affects more than 500 million people worldwide , is caused by damage to cartilage that cushions the ends of bones, resulting in pain, stiffness and inflammation. Standard treatments include painkillers and anti-inflammatory drugs that can ease symptoms. “But many people see little or no benefit,” says Philip Conaghan at the University of Leeds, UK, who wasn’t involved in the latest review. Read more There are only a few anti-ageing supplements that actually work Turmeric supplements are often touted as an alternative therapy. They contain curcumin, a compound that gives turmeric its yellow colour and is thought to have anti-inflammatory properties. Yet such beliefs are often based on prior flawed studies , says Ivan Shirinsky at the Research Institute of Internal and Preventive Medicine in Novosibirsk, Russia. Advertisement Shirinsky and his colleagues analysed results from four randomised controlled trials, collectively involving more than 370 participants with knee osteoarthritis. Participants were randomly assigned to take either a supplement containing turmeric extract or placebo pills two or three times per day, for between eight weeks and three months. Each trial used a slightly different supplement containing a different curcumin dose. “We looked at the most rigorous evidence available,” says Shirinsky. Among those who took a placebo, knee pain decreased by 1.6 points, on average, on a scale from 0 to 10 by the end of the study. Those taking turmeric supplements experienced an average 2.3-point decrease in pain, meaning the difference between the turmeric and placebo groups was half that required to be meaningful to patients based on prior studies , says Shirinsky. science.description: null Astronomers may have, for the first time ever, directly witnessed a star engulfing its companion, a new study reports. As stars die, they swell up to hundreds of times their original size, consuming anything orbiting nearby. In a binary star system, this can include a dying star merging with its companion star. However, scientists had never directly seen any examples of such a cosmic drama unfolding — until now. "Catching a star engulfing its companion in the act is very difficult," study lead author Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University in New York, told Space.com. "When a star engulfs its companion, its effect is very subtle — like throwing a bucket of water in a large ocean. We need sensitive telescopes monitoring the sky for a long time in order to catch this effect." In December 2025, observations from NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope provided the final evidence that allowed researchers to fully reconstruct what happened before, during, and after the merger of a binary star system nicknamed Bao in the Andromeda galaxy. (Image credit: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Viraj Karambelkar (Columbia), Kishalay De (Columbia); Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan (STScI); Acknowledgment: DSS, Robert Gendler) In the new study, the researchers investigated a red giant star designated WNTR23bzdiq, which is located about 2.5 million light-years away in the Andromeda galaxy . The star is about seven times heftier and 350 times wider than our own sun . In 2023, using NASA's now-defunct NEOWISE space telescope and the WINTER telescope at Palomar Observatory in California, the scientists noticed that this star was brightening. By analyzing previous records, they found that the red giant had gradually started growing more luminous in 2018. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 18, 2013: NASA launches MAVEN spacecraft to Mars to find out how the Red Planet lost its water
science.description: null On Nov. 18, 2013, NASA launched the MAVEN spacecraft to Mars. The name of NASA's MAVEN spacecraft stands for Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN. The spacecraft was an orbiter designed to help scientists figure out what happened to the water on Mars and its atmosphere. Mars is dry today, but it data from several Mars missions suggest that it was a much wetter environment a long time ago. MAVEN tracked the rate of atmospheric loss from Mars . The planet has a super thin atmosphere that has been leaking into space for a few billion years. Scientists think that when Mars lost its atmosphere, water dried up on the surface as a result. Solar storms that blast radiation into the solar system appear to have blasted away some of the atmosphere. Carbon dioxide in the atmosphere once kept Mars warm enough to sustain liquid water on its surface , and losing that greenhouse gas turned Mars into a cold and dry place. An Atlas V rocket launches NASA's Mars MAVEN orbiter into space from Florida's Cape Canaveral Space Force Base on Nov. 18, 2013. (Image credit: NASA/Bill Ingalls) Why it mattered NASA's MAVEN spacecraft was the first Mars orbiter ever built to measure how the Martian atmosphere interacts with solar wind , as well as how that constant stream of particles from the sun slowly stripped the Red Planet of its precious atmosphere over time. After its launch in 2013, MAVEN spent about 10 months en route to Mars before entering orbit on Sept. 21, 2014 . The spacecraft then spent the better part of 11 years studying the Red Planet from orbit using three different suites of instruments: An imaging ultraviolet spectrograph to study the global characteristics of the Martian atmosphere; a Neutral Gas and Ion Mass Spectromenter to measure its composition; and a six-instrument setup to study how Mars' ionosphere reacts to solar wind. An artist's view of NASA's MAVEN spacecraft at Mars on a mission to study its upper atmosphere. (Image credit: NASA) "The science MAVEN has given us is key to informing what kind of radiation protection and safety measures we must take before sending humans to Mars," Louise Prockter, NASA director of planetary science, said in June 2026 after the mission concluded. "The data collected from MAVEN will continue to provide valuable insight into Mars for decades to come." MAVEN was originally designed to study Mars for 1 full Earth year after arriving at the Red Planet. That mission ended in 2016, but the spacecraft managed to survive for another 10 years adding more observations for scientists to study. NASA ultimately began using MAVEN as a communications relay for other missions at Mars as the orbiter aged. In December 2025, MAVEN went silent , with NASA losing communication with the orbiter. science.title: Earth is missing over a billion years of geological history. Scientists may have discovered why
science.description: null More than a billion years of Earth's history has seemingly vanished. Across the planet, ancient rock formations contain colossal gaps in the geological record, leaving scientists puzzled over what happened to the missing chapters of our planet's past. Now, researchers believe they may have found an explanation, and the answer lies deep inside Earth . Normally, layers of sediment build up over time, eventually forming sedimentary rocks that preserve clues about our planet's past. Older layers generally lie beneath younger ones, allowing geologists to reconstruct ancient environments and understand how Earth has changed over billions of years. But the geological record isn't always so neatly arranged. In the Grand Canyon, rock layers separated by hundreds of millions of years sit directly on top of one another, revealing a vast gap in Earth's geological record. (Image credit: Marcia Straub via Getty Images) One of the most striking examples is found in the Grand Canyon, where rocks separated by hundreds of millions of years sit directly on top of one another, as if some force or phenomenon removed the layers that geologists would expect to see in between. This enormous gap in Earth's geological timeline is part of the phenomenon known as the Great Unconformity. It's not just the Grand Canyon. Similar gaps have been identified across Europe, Australia, Africa and Asia. Depending on the location, the missing interval ranges from approximately 200 million years to more than a billion years. "Imagine a book where a huge section in the middle has been ripped out," study lead author Santosh Dhungana said in a statement . "The Great Unconformity is that gap in Earth's story, with the narrative jumping from the early chapters straight to a much later part of the story. Our research suggests these pages weren't lost by chance." The Great Unconformity imaged here shows 550 million year old Tapeats Sandstone resting on 1.7 billion year old Vishnu Schist, in Blacktail Canyon along the Colorado River in Grand Canyon National Park, Arizona. (Image credit: William Dummitt via Getty Images) What erased the geological record? Everyone has stress about something – some people love the holidays, and some people are holiday-avoidant… and some live in the middle. What specific stressors or challenges you experience might not bother your sibling, your spouse or your coworker. We want to be aware of and have a clear understanding of what holidays mean to you as a person. science.title: NASA Announces Mid-Power Electric Rocket Challenge for US Companies
science.description: 2 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) The Hall thruster is part of an Solar Electric Propulsion (SEP) system that uses 10 times less propellant than equivalent chemical rockets. Image Credit: NASA/Michelle M. Murphy (Wyle Information Systems, LLC) NASA launched a new competition inviting U.S. companies to produce prototypes of mid-power Hall effect thrusters – a type of electric propulsion system considered crucial for future space operations and exploration. Hall effect thrusters use an electric field to accelerate a propellant gas, producing efficient thrust for long-duration missions. Used for propelling satellites and deep space robotic vehicles, Hall effect thruster systems are critical technology. NASA’s Advanced Mid-Power Electric Rocket (AMPERE) Challenge is offering $500,000, split between two winning U.S. companies, to accelerate the maturation of mid-power systems that could be foundational to supporting future NASA and commercial missions. Interested parties can learn more at an AMPERE Virtual Industry Day hosted by NASA on Thursday, Nov. 19. “This challenge approach seeks to remove key barriers and facilitate commercialization by providing access to NASA subject matter expertise, state-of-the-art technologies, and world-class facilities at no cost to challenge winners,” said Dr. Jason Frieman, AMPERE project co-owner at NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland. “We hope participants will see this as an opportunity to demonstrate their capabilities to NASA and other government and commercial stakeholders.” The competition is the first of NASA’s Tech Maturation Prize series, which seeks to accelerate development of breakthrough technologies in support of NASA missions while strengthening the U.S. space economy. The competition includes three phases. In Phase 1, each participating team will submit a concept design, manufacturing plan, and cost and performance projections. NASA may select two winners to advance to Phase 2, where teams will develop prototypes and collaborate with NASA personnel. Through no-cost licensing, these teams can gain early access to NASA-developed Hall effect thruster technologies that use krypton as a propellant. In Phase 3, prototypes will be tested at NASA Glenn at no cost to the participating teams. In total, two winning teams may be selected to receive up to $250,000 each. The AMPERE Challenge is open for registration until Jan. 27, 2027, at 5 p.m. EST. The challenge supports the Advanced Mid-Power Electric Rocket project, managed by NASA Glenn and NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California. science.title: New Scientist is 70 years old – join us in celebrating
science.description: Julianna Funk/Alamy Break open the bubbly, light the candles and get ready to party – New Scientist is 70 years old! Times have certainly changed since we published our first issue in 1956. Back then, some scientists had proposed that our carbon dioxide emissions were warming the planet, but the idea was controversial. Biologists were only beginning to unpick how DNA, whose structure had just been elucidated by Francis Crick, James Watson, Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins, encoded the instructions for building organisms. The founders of this magazine couldn’t have envisaged the many ways that the web and smartphones would change daily life. We are even old enough that what once seemed futuristic is now pleasantly quaint. Launching our first website, Planet Science , in 1995, we declared that, “As the technologies mature, quite soon and at a terminal near you, it may be possible to hear interviews with well-known scientists”. Our digital offering has expanded greatly since then, with these sorts of interviews now available across our podcast and video channels. That said, we also speculated that it might be possible to “manipulate three-dimensional models of molecules” on a future version of our website, which we still haven’t quite managed to deliver. To mark our anniversary, we have put together a timeline of the biggest breakthroughs of the past 70 years . I enjoyed diving into our archives in search of how we reported era-defining moments. Our assessments haven’t always been on the money: after Yuri Gagarin’s space flight in 1961, for example, our correspondent declared “it is almost physically impossible for [the US] to beat the Russians to the moon”. But looking ahead is in New Scientist ‘s DNA, so, bravely – or foolishly – we press on.
